## Source: amazon-inspector (902667539b73c8560743b0096ebceef827bca34032654378bf852726b7069302)
The package registers an Etherpad `expressPreSession` hook that mounts an undocumented route `GET /Nx_31521/` on the host Etherpad server. The handler responds to any unauthenticated remote caller with an HTML page branded 'Nxploited | Nx-zD' disclosing host identity information read via Node's `os`/`process` APIs: `os.hostname()`, `os.userInfo().username`, `os.platform()`, `process.version`, `process.cwd()`, and `process.pid`. The route is not described in any plugin documentation, has no authentication or access control, and the branding is consistent with an unauthorized marker/defacement rather than a legitimate diagnostic feature. Installing this plugin into an Etherpad instance exposes server reconnaissance data to arbitrary internet callers.
